slice.name: fail-closed replay of durable denial evidence through Chat-native GitHub repository transport
slice.tested_scope: Read an existing immutable role-local denial artifact through the current Chat-exposed GitHub contents surface and mechanically apply a conservative downstream acceptance guard. The guard must preserve the artifact's explicit unresolved/denied state rather than treating durable transport/readability as acceptance evidence. This tests only semantic fail-closed replay of already-durable denial evidence; it does not simulate an authentic GitHub write denial or rate-limit event.

acceptance_guard.rule: ACCEPT only if accepted_phase1_route is explicitly true and no hard unresolved condition remains; otherwise DENY_PHASE1_ACCEPTANCE.

assessment.claim: Within the exact tested repository-transport scope, an immutable denial/unresolved audit survives Chat-native GitHub readback without becoming a false positive when a conservative acceptance guard consumes its explicit fields.

continuation.next_action: On the next reproducibility_auditor invocation, test exactly one still-unproven failure boundary for an already-audited Chat-native route. Prefer an authentic naturally occurring GitHub write denial/missing write surface or rate-limit/resume event if present. If none occurs, use a different existing role-local failure artifact to test one non-duplicative deterministic fail-closed boundary. Do not repeat the transport creation, cross-invocation readback, fail-open-configuration denial, or this denial-replay guard. Keep production idempotency and authentic rate-limit recovery unresolved unless directly evidenced.
